en.title: AI + Art: To Make AI Act Like a Veteran Performer, Acting It Out Yourself Beats Writing More Prompts | Shared by Cheng Jiawei, Founder and Director of Qidian Chuanyue
en.summary:
This article is 2,026 Chinese characters long — about a 7-minute read.

Generative AI is reshaping the film and TV production pipeline, and its core value lies in lowering the bar for validating creative ideas rather than simply boosting efficiency. Cheng Jiawei's team has found in practice that live-action performance references drive AI-generated micro-expressions more reliably than text prompts alone; AI assistance works best when scripts and prompts are locked down first and then handed to an Agent for batch execution; synchronized audio-video generation and smart editing are already practical, but spatial coherence and copyright compliance remain key bottlenecks.

Key points: recording a live performance beats writing prompts; script and prompt templates must be locked in before batch generation; synchronized audio-video and smart editing are already shipping, but spatial consistency and licensing risk remain unresolved.

Suited to film and TV AI tool developers, independent creators, and AIGC content production teams.

Cheng pointed out that if you want AI to perform nuanced emotion, you're better off acting it out yourself than endlessly revising prompts. He shared a practical method his team uses: record a live performance as reference and let AI follow it to handle micro-expressions and movement — more stable and more controllable than text descriptions alone.

en.title: Google's SynthID Detector simplifies watermark detection and expands support to other AI providers
en.summary:
Google DeepMind has announced that SynthID Detector is now available worldwide. The tool is designed to help identify AI-generated content, including media created with AI tools from SynthID partners such as OpenAI, NVIDIA and Kakao, with Apple expected to offer support soon.

SynthID Detector is a cross-vendor AI-generated content detection tool from Google DeepMind, supporting content that uses the SynthID watermarking adopted by OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao and, soon, Apple, and offering a unified upload and binary-verdict interface.

It only detects media with SynthID watermarking integrated, and is not compatible with other watermarking schemes such as those from Meta or Microsoft; large-scale editing weakens the watermark signal, producing a "no clear signal" result; it is not a general-purpose detector and needs to be combined with other tools to form a detection chain.

Suited to content safety work
en.reason: Google DeepMind's SynthID Detector is now globally available, giving a yes-or-no verdict on uploaded files watermarked via OpenAI, NVIDIA, Kakao and soon Apple, but not Meta or Microsoft, and heavy editing can weaken the signal.

en.title: AI + Science: Agents accelerate research—papers get written faster, but the results become harder to evaluate | Wang Huan, PhD advisor at Westlake University's School of Engineering, shares
en.summary:
Word count: 5,339
Reading time: about 18 minutes

Wang Huan examines the dual impact of AI agents on accelerating research workflows and disrupting evaluation systems, from the paired perspectives of efficient AI and AI evaluation. He notes that agents are significantly boosting research efficiency in areas such as literature screening and code writing, but that faster paper output has not brought a corresponding advance in scientific understanding—instead it has intensified the strain on judging credibility and on peer review.

Agents sharply improve research execution efficiency, such as automatically pushing 10 relevant papers per day;
Mass-produced papers erode the depth of scientific validation, making it harder to judge reliability and innovation;
The push for "slow science" is in fundamental tension with current quantitative evaluation systems.
Suitable for AI systems engineers, research computing platform architects, and designers of academic evaluation mechanisms.

Wang Huan has two main research directions: Efficient AI, focused on improving AI's operating efficiency and reducing resource consumption; and AI Evaluation, focused on how to define and measure intelligence.

云电脑正从人类远程办公终端演进为智能体（Agent）的专属运行工位，提供持续执行、权限可控、人机协同的桌面环境。

适合AI架构师、企业级Agent平台开发者、云基础设施工程师阅读。

en.title: AI + the office: Agents now have their own "workstations" — cloud computers let them take over business tasks while keeping permissions in check | Zhang Xiantao, Vice President of R&D at Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group, shares
en.summary:
Word count: 4,839
Reading time: ~16 minutes

Cloud computers are evolving from remote-work terminals for humans into dedicated workstations for agents—desktop environments that offer continuous execution, controllable permissions, and human-agent collaboration.

They let agents invoke desktop software and legacy GUI systems, breaking free of pure API dependence; unify control over identity, permissions, and operation auditing; and establish a seamless human-agent task handoff mechanism.

Intended for AI architects, enterprise agent platform developers, and cloud infrastructure engineers.

At the main forum of the 1024 Model Power Factory · AI Community Day, Zhang Xiantao, Vice President of R&D at Alibaba Cloud Intelligence Group and head of its Terminal Intelligent Computing Division, spoke on "The Evolution of Cloud Computers: From Human Office Desktops to Agent Workstations," sharing the cloud computer's new role in the agent era: giving agents a work environment where they can run continuously, operate within controllable permissions, and collaborate with people.

Zhang joined Alibaba Cloud in 2014, long leading Elastic Compute Service (ECS) before turning to business exploration that combines terminal devices with AI. From supporting workloads in the cloud to providing environments where agents can operate software, his focus has followed suit: as agents enter enterprise workflows, how do you make sure they can get the work done?

在 10 月 22 日举行的 InfoQ AI 侦察团 @QCon 上海 2026 活动中，四位侦察团成员分享了各自企业的 AI 实践进展、面临的挑战与下一步计划。有的企业已将 AI 融入日常工作，另一些则开始思考如何推动 AI 从个人提效走向组织协同，还有的企业正在探索客户沟通数据整合、财务报销自动化等具体场景。

items.title: 最近我一直在琢磨一个事儿：AI Agent 到底还能怎么卷？ 看了一圈各路大模型的更新，天天都在卷参数、卷推理速度、卷谁更聪明。 但说实话， @termix_ai 光停留在“帮人类写写代码、做做表格”这个层面，想象空间其实已经被压得很窄了。 真正的分水岭，绝对不是看它能帮人类打多少工，而是看它什么时候能自己支棱起来，变成一个独立的、能赚钱的商业个体。 这几天关注到搞的方向，刚好戳中了这个点。 从“打工人”到“老板”，AI 的角色变了…

en.title: Recommending a new @ManningBooks book, Domain-Specific Small Language Models: Efficient AI for Local Deployment by Guglielmo Iozzia, out May 2026. The book argues that for domain-specific tasks, the sheer capacity of large models can sometimes be counterproductive.
en.reason: Guglielmo Iozzia's 15-chapter Manning book, due May 2026, walks through fine-tuning, quantization, domain generation and deployment serving including ONNX, arguing that small models trained on domain data can deliver high-quality vertical-task results on ordinary hardware where oversized models sometimes get in the way.

本文字数：2031 字

AI 工具越来越多，企业推进 AI 的方式也在不断变化。但从企业管理者和一线实践者的视角看，AI 落地并能简单地采购工具、开通账号，再等待效率自然提升。
在 10 月 22 日举行的 InfoQ AI 侦察团 @QCon 上海 2026 活动中，四位侦察团成员分享了各自企业的 AI 实践进展、面临的挑战与下一步计划。有的企业已将 AI 融入日常工作，另一些则开始思考如何推动 AI 从个人提效走向组织协同，还有的企业正在探索客户沟通数据整合、财务报销自动化等具体场景。
这些真实具体的实践，给我们提供了观察企业 AI 落地的多维视角。
在研发实践中，AI 正在改变个人完成工作的方式。
来自 TGO 鲲鹏会的朱凯迪在采访中提到，一个人可以借助 AI 串联多个系统、并行推进任务，减少过去跨系统、跨团队协作中的部分沟通摩擦。他还分享了利用 AI 重构早年搁置的 C++ 游戏引擎项目的尝试：在提前梳理项目结构、技术要求和性能约束后，他使用 AI 在几个小时内推进了原本因工作量较大而搁置的项目，完成效果也让他感到满意。
